finding: The EOF comparison used (sector + n) * 512 in u32, allowing overflow to admit requests beyond the file. Unchecked cluster shifts could be undefined, and nonempty NULL output could reach SD I/O.
change: Use complete-sector count and subtraction-based bounds. Reject shift counts >=32 and nonempty NULL output before calculating cluster size or touching I/O. Preserve legal zero-length requests and existing cluster/contiguous-run behavior.
verification: check_scsd_file_read_bounds.py: independent 64-bit EOF oracle across 27000 size/position/count/cluster/layout/NULL combinations, plus large overflow and shift boundaries
Controlled mapping/SD I/O verifies source sectors, cluster split lengths, destination offsets, output data and canaries
Mid-read mapping and I/O failures stop subsequent operations, preserving the unwritten suffix
Baseline e2ce7b1 fails both the full fixture and isolated overflow cases; current source passes both
Existing FAT directory fixture still passes; GNU ARM compilation of src/hack_scsd.c passes without diagnostics
limitations: Controlled mapping and SD I/O. Accepted reads larger than the fixture output buffer are not executed. Caller buffer capacity, mount validation, physical LBA bounds, cluster-chain integrity and real hardware remain unverified. Failed multi-run reads may retain the successfully read prefix, as before.
